job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Meera noticed her friend Rohan felt tired during football practice, and his skin looked pale. Their teacher, Mrs. Sharma, explained that these symptoms might suggest anaemia, a condition where the blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen. She clarified that anaemia is not a contagious disease that spreads like a cold, nor is it only a problem for girls. Mrs. Sharma emphasised that haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, requires iron to function properly. She advised them to eat a balanced diet including green leafy vegetables like spinach, lentils, and nuts, explaining that while meat is a good source, plant-based foods also provide essential iron. When Rohan asked if he should just take iron tablets instead of eating healthy food, Mrs. Sharma shook her head. She explained that tablets are supplements, but the body absorbs iron best from a variety of natural foods. Furthermore, she warned that eating excessive iron is not helpful, as the body only absorbs what it needs. Finally, she mentioned that Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits, helps the body absorb iron more efficiently, though the vitamin itself does not contain iron. By eating a diverse diet, both boys and girls can maintain healthy haemoglobin levels and stay energetic.

items.evidence: She clarified that anaemia is not a contagious disease that spreads like a cold, nor is it only a problem for girls.
items.q: Meera worries she will catch anaemia from Rohan. What should Mrs. Sharma tell her?
options: It does not pass from person to person
It passes on through coughs, like a cold
It passes on only to girls, not boys
It passes on only when someone is very sick
items.explain: Anaemia is not contagious like a cold, so Meera cannot catch it from Rohan.

wrong.why: thinks anaemia spreads like a cold
thinks anaemia is only a girls' problem
thinks anaemia matters only when someone is very sick

items.evidence: Mrs. Sharma emphasised that haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, requires iron to function properly.
items.q: Why can too little iron make Rohan feel tired during football?
options: His blood cannot carry enough oxygen
His blood loses its red food colour
His haemoglobin stops making energy itself
His body has run out of blood
items.explain: Haemoglobin needs iron to carry oxygen; with less iron, less oxygen reaches his body.

wrong.why: thinks blood is red from food colour
thinks haemoglobin makes energy by itself
thinks anaemia means too little blood

items.evidence: She advised them to eat a balanced diet including green leafy vegetables like spinach, lentils, and nuts, explaining that while meat is a good source, plant-based foods also provide essential iron.
items.q: Rohan is vegetarian. How can he get enough iron?
options: By eating leafy greens, dal and nuts
By drinking lots of milk every day
By eating spinach just once to cure it
By adding meat, since plants have no iron
items.explain: Plant foods like leafy greens, lentils and nuts also give essential iron, not only meat.

wrong.why: thinks milk is best for preventing anaemia
thinks one meal of spinach cures anaemia

items.evidence: Furthermore, she warned that eating excessive iron is not helpful, as the body only absorbs what it needs.
items.q: Rohan eats three times his usual iron to get healthy faster. What happens?
options: The extra iron will not help him more
The extra iron will make him much healthier
The extra iron will cure him in one day
The extra iron will turn his blood redder
items.explain: Too much iron is not helpful because the body takes in only what it needs.

wrong.why: thinks more iron is always better
thinks a big dose cures anaemia instantly
thinks blood is red from iron rust

items.evidence: Finally, she mentioned that Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits, helps the body absorb iron more efficiently, though the vitamin itself does not contain iron.
items.q: Why might eating an orange with dal help Rohan?
options: The orange helps his body use dal's iron
The orange adds its own iron to the dal
The orange works instead of iron-rich foods
The orange is a complete food, like milk
items.explain: Vitamin C in citrus fruits helps the body absorb iron, though it has no iron itself.

wrong.why: thinks a helper can replace iron foods
thinks a complete food prevents anaemia
